rows.title: [Feature] Add search pets by name screen
rows.excerpt:
## Summary

Add a new screen that allows users to search for pets by name, similar to the existing "Find Owners" functionality.

## Motivation

- Currently there is no way to search for a pet directly by name; users must first find the owner and then browse their pets.
- A dedicated pet search screen would improve usability when the pet name is known but the owner is not.
- Aligns the pet entity with the same search UX pattern already established for owners.

## Proposed Solution

1. **New Thymeleaf template** (`templates/pets/findPets.html`) with a search form and results list/table.
2. **New controller** endpoint(s) in a `PetController` (or extend existing controller) to handle `GET /pets/find` and `GET /pets` with a `name` query parameter.
3. **New repository method** `findByNameContainingIgnoreCase(String name)` (or equivalent Spring Data query) in `PetRepository`.
4. **Navigation link** added to the main layout so users can access the pet search screen.
5. **Accessibility**: the new page must meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA (keyboard navigation, visible focus, proper labels, contrast, landmarks, etc.).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A "Find Pets" link is available in the main navigation menu
- [ ] Users can search for pets by entering a full or partial pet name (case-insensitive)
- [ ] An empty search returns all pets
- [ ] Search results display pet name, birth date, type, and owner name
- [ ] Clicking a result navigates to the pet's or owner's detail page
- [ ] The page is accessible (landmarks, labels, keyboard support, contrast)
- [ ] Unit and integration tests cover the new controller and repository methods
- [ ] Works with H2 (default), MySQL, and PostgreSQL profiles

## Alternatives Considered

- Extending the existing owner search to also filter by pet name — rejected because it conflates two different search intents.

## Additional Context

The implementation should follow the same patterns used by the existing "Find Owners" feature (`OwnerController`, `findOwners.html`, `ownersList.html`).

rows.title: Documentation: Improve documentation across classes
rows.excerpt:
## Summary
This PR improves documentation across three core classes in the PetClinic application as part of the sustainable coding practices evaluation for SE754 Assignment 5.

## Problem
Manual review and SonarQube feedback showed that several important classes in the owner and vet areas were under-documented. While the code was functional, the intent of the domain objects and controller flows was not immediately clear to readers, especially around model preparation, pet ownership rules, and veterinarian specialty handling.

The `Owner` domain model, `PetController`, and `Vet` model each contain logic that benefits from clearer class-level and method-level documentation. Without that context, future contributors have to infer behavior from implementation details rather than from the API contract.

## Changes
- Expanded the class-level documentation in `Owner.java` to explain its role as the core owner entity and its relationship to pets
- Added method-level documentation in `PetController.java` to clarify:
  - model attribute preparation
  - request binding
  - validation flow
  - pet create/update handling
- Improved the class and method documentation in `Vet.java` to explain:
  - specialty management
  - the read-only sorted view exposed to callers

## Sustainability Impact
Better documentation reduces cognitive load for future maintenance work. These classes are part of the main application flow, so clearer comments and Javadoc help new contributors understand why the code exists, not just what it does.

This improves long-term maintainability by:
- reducing onboarding friction for new contributors
- making controller and domain behavior easier to reason about
- lowering the risk of incorrect future modifications
- improving overall code readability and maintainability

## Files Changed
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/Owner.java`
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/PetController.java`
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/Vet.java`

rows.title: All visits section added
rows.excerpt: ## Summary This PR adds a dedicated page to display all visits associated with a specific pet. Previously, visit history was displayed only on the Owner Details page. With this change, users can click the **"All Visits"** link for a pet to navigate to a separate page containing the complete visit history. ## Changes - Added an **"All Visits"** link for each pet on the Owner Details page. - Added a new controller endpoint to handle viewing all visits for a pet. - Created a new Thymeleaf template to display the visit history. - Added navigation back to the Owner Details page. ## Screenshots ### Before ### After ## Testing - Verified that the "All Visits" link opens the correct page. - Verified that only visits for the selected pet are displayed. - Verified navigation back to the Owner Details page

rows.title: Delete functionality for Owners
rows.excerpt: Description: - Adds the ability to delete an Owner from the Owner details page, along with all associated Pets and Visits (cascade delete). Changes: - Added deleteOwner() handler in OwnerController (POST /owners/{ownerId}/delete) - Added delete(Owner) to OwnerRepository - Added "Delete Owner" button to ownerDetails.html, with a JS confirm dialog to prevent accidental deletion - Cascade delete relies on existing CascadeType.ALL mapping on Owner.pets and Pet.visits - Added Javadoc comments for the new controller method and repository method Tests: - Verified successful delete redirects to /owners/find with a flash success message - Verified the correct Owner (with pets) is passed to delete() - Verified deleting a non-existent owner throws/returns an error, and delete() is never called - Verified GET on the delete endpoint is rejected (405)
